Long Man of Wilmington.alt: An early eighteenth-century antiquarian sketches the enormous white outline of the Long Man on Windover Hill
Long Man of Wilmington.caption: A visual interpretation of the Long Man around the time of its earliest surviving record
Long Man of Wilmington.pullquote: Its age and meaning are genuine mysteries.
Long Man of Wilmington.seo_title: Long Man of Wilmington: Sussex's Chalk Giant · Folklore Finder

Zennor.alt: The carved medieval mermaid bench-end inside St Senara Church at Zennor in soft Cornish daylight
Zennor.caption: A visual interpretation of the mermaid bench-end at St Senara Church, Zennor
Zennor.pullquote: Ships in the cove are said to sometimes hear Trewhella's voice rising from the water, still singing.

Wayland the Smith.alt: Wayland's Smithy at dawn with an unshod horse waiting beside the Neolithic barrow on the Ridgeway
Wayland the Smith.caption: A visual interpretation of Wayland the Smith at Wayland's Smithy on the Ridgeway
Wayland the Smith.pullquote: Tradition, already old when the Saxons named the place, held that a traveller whose horse had cast a shoe need only leave the beast there with a coin overnight, and by morning the unseen smith would have shod it.
Wayland the Smith.seo_title: Wayland the Smith: Britain's Legendary Smith · Folklore Finder

Old Man of Storr.alt: The black basalt pinnacle of the Old Man of Storr rising above wet grass on Skye with sea beyond
Old Man of Storr.caption: A visual interpretation of the Old Man of Storr on the Trotternish Ridge
Old Man of Storr.pullquote: When the giant died and was buried in the hillside, his thumb was left protruding above the ground, and there it has stood ever since, weathering into the jagged spire seen today.

Fachan.alt: The one-eyed, one-legged Fachan crossing a rain-dark track in Glen Etive beneath heavy Highland cloud
Fachan.caption: A visual interpretation of the Fachan in Glen Etive
Fachan.section_heading: The straight one of Glen Etive
Fachan.pullquote: It is a being of terrible single-ness: one eye in the middle of its face, one hand reaching from its chest, one leg beneath it, and a single tuft of dark feathers or hair on its head.

Cu Sith.alt: The shaggy green Cu Sith crossing a wet Skye moor at dusk with its tail curled high above the heather
Cu Sith.caption: A visual interpretation of the Cu Sith on the moors of Skye
Cu Sith.pullquote: Those bays were a death-warning: anyone who heard them and failed to reach safety before the third was said to be overcome, or carried off.

Dando's Dogs.alt: A dark rider and pack of hounds driving along a storm-struck Cornish track at dusk
Dando's Dogs.caption: A visual interpretation of Dando's spectral hunt in Cornwall
Dando's Dogs.pullquote: Ever since, the country folk said, Dando and his dogs may be heard on stormy nights sweeping across the Cornish sky and moors in a spectral hunt, the baying of the hounds carrying on the wind.

Beltane Fire Festival.alt: Torch-bearing Beltane participants and drummers processing across Calton Hill above Edinburgh at night
Beltane Fire Festival.caption: A visual interpretation of the modern Beltane procession on Calton Hill
Beltane Fire Festival.pullquote: Though a contemporary creation rather than an unbroken survival, it consciously revives the imagery and meaning of the old Beltane.

Duergar.alt: A lone traveller on the Simonside Hills approaching a false lantern light near a crouching Duergar at the cliff edge
Duergar.caption: A visual interpretation of the Duergar luring a traveller on the Simonside Hills
Duergar.pullquote: The Simonside Hills kept their reputation as a place no wise man crossed after dark.

Finfolk.alt: Two dark Finfolk sea-sorcerers in a narrow boat off a rocky Orkney shore at dusk
Finfolk.caption: A visual interpretation of Finfolk nearing the Orkney shore
Finfolk.pullquote: They steal mortals for spouses and servants.

Tom Hickathrift.alt: Tom Hickathrift facing the giant of the Marshland with a cart wheel and axle on a muddy Fenland causeway
Tom Hickathrift.caption: A visual interpretation of Tom Hickathrift fighting the giant of the Marshland
Tom Hickathrift.section_heading: The giant on the marsh road
Tom Hickathrift.pullquote: Tom upended his cart, took the axle for a club and a wheel for a shield, and beat the giant to death, winning his hoard and his land for the people.

Mary Butters, the Carnmoney Witch.alt: Mary Butters tending a smoking pot of milk and nails inside a dark County Antrim farmhouse while a man stands watch outside the door
Mary Butters, the Carnmoney Witch.caption: A visual interpretation of Mary Butters performing the Carnmoney bewitchment cure
Mary Butters, the Carnmoney Witch.section_heading: The night of the smoke cure
Mary Butters, the Carnmoney Witch.pullquote: She sealed a farmhouse in foul smoke to perform her rite and two people were found dead by dawn.

Bardney Abbey and the Light of Oswald.alt: Monks at Bardney Abbey watching a pale pillar of light rise from King Oswald's bier outside the timber gate at night
Bardney Abbey and the Light of Oswald.caption: A visual interpretation of the miracle at Bardney Abbey
Bardney Abbey and the Light of Oswald.pullquote: During the night, according to Bede, a pillar of light rose from the body of Oswald and blazed upward into the sky, visible across all the surrounding countryside.

Metheringham Lass.alt: A young WAAF woman raising a hand on a rain-dark Lincolnshire road with the distant lights of RAF Metheringham behind her
Metheringham Lass.caption: A visual interpretation of the Metheringham Lass on the road by RAF Metheringham
Metheringham Lass.pullquote: The young woman is said to be accompanied by a strong, sweet smell of lavender as she pleads for help.

Wayland's Smithy.alt: A saddled horse standing beside the stones of Wayland's Smithy at dawn with a silver coin left on the capstone
Wayland's Smithy.caption: A visual interpretation of Wayland's Smithy on the Ridgeway
Wayland's Smithy.pullquote: It was said that if a traveller's horse had cast a shoe, he need only leave the horse beside the barrow together with a silver coin upon the capstone.
Wayland's Smithy.seo_title: Wayland's Smithy: A Legendary Smith's Forge · Folklore Finder

Hobby Horse of Padstow.alt: The black Obby Oss moving through a whitewashed Padstow street with its Teaser and musicians on May Day
Hobby Horse of Padstow.caption: A visual interpretation of the Obby Oss in Padstow on May Day
Hobby Horse of Padstow.pullquote: From dawn the streets ring with the 'Morning Song', and two great hobby horses - the 'Old' 'Oss and the 'Blue Ribbon' 'Oss - caper through the town.

Chûn Quoit.alt: Chûn Quoit standing on open Cornish moorland beneath heavy Atlantic cloud with the sea in the distance
Chûn Quoit.caption: A visual interpretation of Chûn Quoit on the moors above west Cornwall
Chûn Quoit.section_heading: The giant's quoit on the downs
Chûn Quoit.pullquote: Giants, the stories say, hurled them into place while playing a game of quoits.

Callanish Standing Stones.alt: The Callanish Standing Stones rising from rough grass beside Loch Roag in soft Hebridean dawn light
Callanish Standing Stones.caption: A visual interpretation of the Callanish stones at dawn on Lewis
Callanish Standing Stones.pullquote: Early on the morning of the summer solstice, a mysterious figure known simply as the Shining One is said to walk the length of the main avenue from north to south.

Branwen.alt: Branwen in early medieval dress holding a starling above the rocky Anglesey shore at dusk
Branwen.caption: A visual interpretation of Branwen sending her message across the sea
Branwen.pullquote: She tamed a starling, taught it speech, and sent it across the sea with word of her misery.

Ellén Trechend.alt: A three-headed beast crawling from the dark mouth of Oweynagat above the fields of Rathcroghan under heavy cloud
Ellén Trechend.caption: A visual interpretation of the Ellén Trechend emerging at Oweynagat
Ellén Trechend.pullquote: A monstrous three-headed creature emerged from the dark cave of Cruachan and rampaged across Ireland.

Nanteos Cup.alt: The worn wooden Nanteos Cup on a dark table beside a window overlooking the hills of Ceredigion
Nanteos Cup.caption: A visual interpretation of the Nanteos Cup at Nanteos Mansion
Nanteos Cup.pullquote: The sick would come to the mansion, take the fragment home on surety of its return, and drink water from it or press it to their ailments.

Pwyll, Prince of Dyfed.alt: Pwyll standing on the Gorsedd Arberth mound while Rhiannon waits on a white horse across the Pembrokeshire pasture
Pwyll, Prince of Dyfed.caption: A visual interpretation of Pwyll witnessing Rhiannon at Gorsedd Arberth
Pwyll, Prince of Dyfed.pullquote: Pwyll sits there and witnesses a woman in gold silk on a white horse circling the mound: Rhiannon.

Queen Medb.alt: Queen Medb standing beside the cairn on Knocknarea above Sligo Bay at dawn
Queen Medb.caption: A visual interpretation of Queen Medb on Knocknarea in County Sligo
Queen Medb.pullquote: Medb is said to be buried standing upright, facing her enemies in Ulster, beneath the great cairn known as Meascan Meabha.

Hartlepool Monkey.alt: A monkey in a miniature French naval uniform standing before Hartlepool fishermen on a wreck-strewn beach
Hartlepool Monkey.caption: A visual interpretation of the Hartlepool monkey legend on the County Durham coast
Hartlepool Monkey.pullquote: The monkey, unable to answer their questions in English, was convicted of espionage and hanged from the mast of the wrecked ship.

Grey Man of Ben MacDhui.alt: A lone walker on the misty summit of Ben Macdui with a vast grey figure suggested in the cloud behind him
Grey Man of Ben MacDhui.caption: A visual interpretation of the Grey Man on Ben Macdui in the Cairngorms
Grey Man of Ben MacDhui.pullquote: Climbers on the lonely plateau have described the unmistakable sound of slow, heavy footsteps crunching behind them in the mist.

Wild Man of Orford.alt: A hairy wild man tangled in fishing nets on the shingle shore below Orford Castle
Wild Man of Orford.caption: A visual interpretation of the Wild Man of Orford on the Suffolk coast
Wild Man of Orford.pullquote: Despite months of captivity and attempts at questioning and torture, he never spoke, communicating only in grunts, and ate raw fish, always wringing out the moisture first.

Isobel Gowdie.alt: Isobel Gowdie standing on rough ground near Auldearn while a hare darts through the grass
Isobel Gowdie.caption: A visual interpretation of Isobel Gowdie near Auldearn in 1662
Isobel Gowdie.pullquote: Gowdie described slipping out of her own body to fly through the night air, feasting with the fairy folk beneath the hills, and riding with the Queen of Elfhame.

Twrch Trwyth.alt: A huge dark boar charging across the Pembrokeshire coast with distant hunters behind
Twrch Trwyth.caption: A visual interpretation of Twrch Trwyth near Porth Clais in Pembrokeshire
Twrch Trwyth.pullquote: Carrying a comb, razor and shears between his ears, the creature lands near Porth Clais and leaves a destructive trail across Wales before fleeing toward Cornwall.

Ascapart.alt: The giant Ascapart striding beside Southampton Water with Bevis and his horse following behind
Ascapart.caption: A visual interpretation of Ascapart on the coast of Southampton Water
Ascapart.pullquote: After Bevis defeats him in single combat, Ascapart does not die. He becomes Bevis's follower and companion, the loyal giant-servant who carries out tasks too large for any human knight.

Dragon of Ludham.alt: A low dark dragon beside Ludham churchyard with St Benet's Abbey distant across the marshes
Dragon of Ludham.caption: A visual interpretation of the Dragon of Ludham in the Norfolk Broads
Dragon of Ludham.pullquote: Furious to find its lair blocked, the dragon thrashed its tail and took to the air, flying along the causeway towards the ruined Abbey of St Benet at Holm.

Wiltshire Moonrakers.alt: Wiltshire smugglers raking a moonlit pond while the reflected moon gleams on the water
Wiltshire Moonrakers.caption: A visual interpretation of the Moonrakers' pond trick in Wiltshire
Wiltshire Moonrakers.pullquote: Smugglers caught raking a moonlit pond told excise men they were fishing for a round cheese, the moon's reflection.

Boobrie.alt: The Boobrie as an enormous black water bird standing over a bloodied carcass at the edge of a storm-dark Argyll loch
Boobrie.caption: A visual interpretation of the Boobrie on a loch in Argyll
Boobrie.pullquote: Its cry, witnesses agreed, was not birdlike at all. It bellowed like a bull.

The Merry Maidens.alt: The granite stones of the Merry Maidens standing in rough Cornish grass beneath a clearing storm sky
The Merry Maidens.caption: A visual interpretation of the Merry Maidens stone circle near St Buryan
The Merry Maidens.pullquote: The stones are said to be young women turned to rock as a punishment for dancing on the Sabbath.

Worm of Linton.alt: The Worm of Linton rearing from its den on Linton Hill as John Somerville advances with a burning lance
Worm of Linton.caption: A visual interpretation of the Worm of Linton in the Scottish Borders
Worm of Linton.pullquote: He thrust the blazing mass down its throat and burned it from within.

Billy Marshall.alt: Billy Marshall standing on a muddy Galloway road beside a small horse and wagon near Kirkcudbright kirkyard under a grey sky
Billy Marshall.caption: A visual interpretation of the Billy Marshall legend in Galloway
Billy Marshall.pullquote: He married seventeen wives and fathered sixty-eight children; tradition insists four were born after his hundredth birthday.

Jack o' Kent.alt: Jack o' Kent standing beside a medieval stone bridge while a dog crosses the River Monnow through morning mist
Jack o' Kent.caption: A visual interpretation of Jack o' Kent in the Welsh Marches
Jack o' Kent.pullquote: He has the Devil build a bridge over the Monnow in a single night in return for the soul of the first to cross it, then sends a dog over first and cheats Satan of his fee.

Knucker of Lyminster.alt: The Knucker of Lyminster rising from a dark spring-fed pool beside a cart and horse at dusk in West Sussex
Knucker of Lyminster.caption: A visual interpretation of the Sussex Knucker legend
Knucker of Lyminster.pullquote: He baked an enormous poisoned pie, carted it out to the Knucker Hole, and let the greedy dragon swallow pie, horse, cart and all.

Cernunnos.alt: An antlered figure in worn Iron Age dress standing in an oak woodland beside a stag at dawn
Cernunnos.caption: A visual interpretation of Cernunnos in a British woodland setting
Cernunnos.pullquote: He is depicted as a mature figure crowned with the antlers of a stag.

Áine.alt: A woman in simple early Irish dress standing on Knockainey at dusk while torchbearers climb the hill behind her
Áine.caption: A visual interpretation of Áine and the midsummer rite at Knockainey
Áine.pullquote: Local families climbed Cnoc Áine carrying torches of hay and straw tied to hazel poles.

Merlin's Cave.alt: A lone cloaked figure standing at the mouth of Merlin's Cave below the cliffs of Tintagel at low tide
Merlin's Cave.caption: A visual interpretation of Merlin's Cave beneath the Tintagel headland
Merlin's Cave.pullquote: Despite the name, no medieval source places Merlin inside, or anywhere near, this cave.

Rollright Stones curse.alt: Weathered standing stones on high Oxfordshire ground at dusk with a dark cloaked figure among them
Rollright Stones curse.caption: A visual interpretation of the Rollright Stones curse in Oxfordshire
Rollright Stones curse.pullquote: They were once a would-be conqueror and his army, turned to stone by a witch.

facts.Motif: King and knights turned to stone

Bomere Fish.alt: A huge pike-like fish breaking the surface of Bomere Pool beside a half-submerged bell at dusk
Bomere Fish.caption: A visual interpretation of the Bomere Fish in the waters of Bomere Pool
Bomere Fish.pullquote: The most famous of its tales concerns a great fish, a pike of monstrous size, said to dwell in its dark waters.

Mermaid of Marden.alt: A dark-haired river spirit in the water hauling a church bell toward the bank of the River Lugg at dusk
Mermaid of Marden.caption: A visual interpretation of the Mermaid of Marden drawing the church bell back into the river
Mermaid of Marden.pullquote: The bell was nearly clear of the water, and a mermaid appeared and seized it back into the depths.

Bisterne Dragon.alt: A medieval knight with two mastiffs facing a dragon on open heath near Burley at dusk
Bisterne Dragon.caption: A visual interpretation of the Bisterne Dragon on the edge of the New Forest
Bisterne Dragon.section_heading: The dragon on the forest edge
Bisterne Dragon.pullquote: the terrified people set out a daily pail of milk to appease it

Penhill Giant.alt: A huge ragged giant striding with a pack of hounds on the slopes of Penhill above Wensleydale
Penhill Giant.caption: A visual interpretation of the Penhill Giant above Wensleydale
Penhill Giant.pullquote: a brutal ogre who kept a pack of savage hounds and lorded it over the shepherds of the dale

Wisht Hounds.alt: A pack of spectral black hounds racing across wet Dartmoor ground with a hooded huntsman behind them
Wisht Hounds.caption: A visual interpretation of the Wisht Hounds near Wistman's Wood on Dartmoor
Wisht Hounds.pullquote: to hear their baying carried on the wind was an omen of death

Helen Duncan.alt: Helen Duncan seated at a wartime seance table in a dim parlour with strips of false ectoplasm hanging from her mouth
Helen Duncan.caption: A visual interpretation of Helen Duncan in a wartime séance room
Helen Duncan.section_heading: The séance that reached the courts
Helen Duncan.pullquote: she appeared to produce 'ectoplasm', a substance said to let spirits take form

Matthew Hopkins.alt: Matthew Hopkins in black Civil War era dress standing beside a muddy Essex pond with accused women and townspeople under watch
Matthew Hopkins.caption: A visual interpretation of Matthew Hopkins at work in Civil War era Essex
Matthew Hopkins.pullquote: the title 'Witchfinder General' was entirely his own invention

Seonaidh.alt: A towering sea spirit rising from kelp-dark water off the coast of Lewis under a stormy dusk sky
Seonaidh.caption: A visual interpretation of Seonaidh emerging from the Atlantic off Lewis
Seonaidh.pullquote: Seonaidh, anglicised as Shony or Shoney, was a sea-spirit or sea-god of the Isle of Lewis

Red Hand of Ulster.alt: An early medieval Irish chieftain in a currach hurling his severed right hand toward the shore on the Ulster coast at dawn
Red Hand of Ulster.caption: A visual interpretation of the race for Ulster's kingship
Red Hand of Ulster.pullquote: As one contestant saw he was losing the race, he drew his blade, severed his own right hand, and flung it onto the strand

Winchester Round Table.alt: The great painted Round Table hanging on the wall of Winchester Great Hall with a lone visitor standing beneath it
Winchester Round Table.caption: A visual interpretation of the Round Table in Winchester Great Hall
Winchester Round Table.pullquote: The table was almost certainly built for one such occasion - a prop in a carefully staged chivalric performance rather than an ancient relic.

Tuatha Dé Danann.alt: Cloaked figures of the Tuatha Dé Danann standing beside a grassy mound in the mist at the Hill of Tara in County Meath
Tuatha Dé Danann.caption: A visual interpretation of the Tuatha Dé Danann in the Irish mythic landscape
Tuatha Dé Danann.pullquote: They retreated underground, into the hollow hills - the sídhe - and became the people of the mounds.

Whiteleaf Cross.alt: The chalk Whiteleaf Cross cut into the steep grassy slope of Whiteleaf Hill above the Buckinghamshire vale
Whiteleaf Cross.caption: A visual interpretation of Whiteleaf Cross on the Chiltern escarpment
Whiteleaf Cross.pullquote: Its date and purpose remain genuinely unknown - first recorded as an antiquity by Francis Wise in 1742, no earlier written reference has ever been found.

Hill of Allen.alt: The Hill of Allen rising above the Bog of Allen with its summit tower under a heavy sky in County Kildare
Hill of Allen.caption: A visual interpretation of the Hill of Allen, seat of Fionn mac Cumhaill
Hill of Allen.pullquote: When Victorian workers built the present stone tower on the summit in 1863, they reported uncovering a massive coffin containing what they took to be the hero's own bones, which they respectfully reinterred on the hilltop.

Dorset Ooser.alt: The horned wooden Dorset Ooser mask hanging in a rustic farm doorway above the Dorset hills
Dorset Ooser.caption: A visual interpretation of the Dorset Ooser of Melbury Osmond
Dorset Ooser.section_heading: The horned mask in the village
Dorset Ooser.pullquote: The mask functioned as the community's anonymous enforcer: a face that was no one's face, delivering a judgement that was everyone's.

La Bête De La Tour.alt: A massive black dog wound in heavy iron chains moving beside a Guernsey coastal tower under stormy skies
La Bête De La Tour.caption: A visual interpretation of Guernsey's Beast of the Tower
La Bête De La Tour.pullquote: a massive black dog whose body is wound in heavy iron chains that clank and rattle as it moves

Plynlimon.alt: The high moorland bulk of Plynlimon rendered as a giant-like massif above dark Welsh river sources under heavy cloud
Plynlimon.caption: A visual interpretation of Plynlimon, father of rivers in Welsh legend
Plynlimon.pullquote: Folklore made the rivers his three daughters: Hafren (Severn), Gwy (Wye) and Rheidol.

The Bute Witches.alt: Four accused women in plain seventeenth-century dress standing under guard near Rothesay on the Isle of Bute
The Bute Witches.caption: A visual interpretation of the Bute witch trials at Rothesay
The Bute Witches.pullquote: she 'soon brought home a little fairy of her own to nurse.'

Windhouse.alt: The roofless stone shell of Windhouse standing above Whale Firth on Yell under a dark Shetland sky
Windhouse.caption: A visual interpretation of haunted Windhouse on Yell
Windhouse.section_heading: The haunted house above the firth
Windhouse.pullquote: Standing isolated above Whale Firth on the island of Yell, the roofless shell of Windhouse has long been called the most haunted building in Shetland.

Witches of Garway Hill.alt: A small group of wise women gathered by a spring below Garway Hill with the Herefordshire church and hill behind them
Witches of Garway Hill.caption: A visual interpretation of the wise women of Garway Hill
Witches of Garway Hill.section_heading: The wise women on the hill
Witches of Garway Hill.pullquote: There'll always be nine witches from the bottom of Orcop to the end of Garway Hill, as long as water runs.

Buckinghamshire Revenant.alt: A medieval revenant standing in a Buckinghamshire churchyard at night while villagers watch from near a doorway
Buckinghamshire Revenant.caption: A visual interpretation of the Buckinghamshire revenant returning from the grave
Buckinghamshire Revenant.pullquote: a scroll of absolution was laid upon the corpse's breast in its reopened grave, and from that hour the dead man walked no more

facts.Motif: Absolution lays the dead to rest

Cyhyraeth.alt: A lone figure listening beside the Welsh coast at night while dark water lies under a bleak sky
Cyhyraeth.caption: A visual interpretation of the Welsh death-cry known as the Cyhyraeth
Cyhyraeth.pullquote: A Welsh death omen: a disembodied wailing voice heard in the dark, always three times, always before a death.

Cú Roí mac Dáire.alt: An early medieval Irish warrior-king standing by the stone ring-fort on Caherconree with the Kerry mountains behind him
Cú Roí mac Dáire.caption: A visual interpretation of Cú Roí mac Dáire at Caherconree
Cú Roí mac Dáire.pullquote: His stronghold is associated with Caherconree in the Slieve Mish Mountains, where legend says his fortress revolved at night so that enemies could not find its entrance.

Devil's Dyke.alt: The deep dry valley of Devil's Dyke cutting through the South Downs under unsettled dawn light
Devil's Dyke.caption: A visual interpretation of the South Downs legend of Devil's Dyke
Devil's Dyke.pullquote: The Devil carved this gash through the South Downs in one night, set on drowning Sussex's churches - a crowing cockerel tricked him into thinking dawn had broken, and he fled mid-dig.

Henderson Stone.alt: A redcoat soldier gesturing beside the Henderson Stone in snowy Glencoe while a Highland man listens
Henderson Stone.caption: A visual interpretation of the Henderson Stone legend in Glencoe
Henderson Stone.pullquote: Great stone of the glen! Great is your right to be here. But if you knew what will happen this night you would be up and away.

Lilias Adie.alt: An elderly woman standing beside the stone slab over Lilias Adie's grave on the Torryburn foreshore at low tide
Lilias Adie.caption: A visual interpretation of Lilias Adie on the Torryburn shore
Lilias Adie.pullquote: She was buried not in consecrated ground but on the foreshore at Torryburn, between the high and low tide marks, with a heavy stone slab placed over the grave.

Tehi Tegi.alt: A dark-haired woman wading through a Manx river while three men follow spellbound behind her
Tehi Tegi.caption: A visual interpretation of Tehi Tegi leading her followers into the river
Tehi Tegi.pullquote: They abandoned homes, farms, and families to trail behind her wherever she walked, and the island fell into ruin.

Gulf of Corryvreckan.alt: The Corryvreckan whirlpool churning beside the dark cliffs between Jura and Scarba under an overcast sky
Gulf of Corryvreckan.caption: A visual interpretation of the Corryvreckan whirlpool off Jura and Scarba
Gulf of Corryvreckan.pullquote: On the third night the rope of maidens' hair broke too, and Breacan was dragged down to his death.

St Catherine's Hill Mizmaze.alt: The rectangular turf mizmaze cut into the chalk summit of St Catherine's Hill beside chapel ruins near Winchester
St Catherine's Hill Mizmaze.caption: A visual interpretation of the Mizmaze on St Catherine's Hill
St Catherine's Hill Mizmaze.section_heading: The boy who carved the maze
St Catherine's Hill Mizmaze.pullquote: A bored Winchester schoolboy carved a turf maze so intricate it broke his mind in the tracing.

Witches' Well.alt: The Witches' Well memorial set into the stone wall on Castlehill in Edinburgh above the Royal Mile
Witches' Well.caption: A visual interpretation of the Edinburgh memorial to accused witches
Witches' Well.pullquote: most of those who suffered were not witches at all but innocent victims of fear and superstition.

Beithir.alt: A huge serpent-dragon rising from Loch Indaal while Islay sailors prepare spiked barrels on the shore
Beithir.caption: A visual interpretation of the Beithir legend on Islay
Beithir.pullquote: sailors killed it using flesh-covered barrels armed with iron spikes.

Bignor Hill Dragon.alt: An ancient dragon coiled around Bignor Hill, its body forming chalk folds above the Sussex landscape
Bignor Hill Dragon.caption: A visual interpretation of the dragon said to shape Bignor Hill
Bignor Hill Dragon.pullquote: its body cutting the folds still visible in the chalk landscape above a Roman villa.

Dragon of Brinsop.alt: Saint George on horseback slaying the Dragon of Brinsop beside the well of Duck Pool meadow
Dragon of Brinsop.caption: A visual interpretation of the Dragon of Brinsop battle near Duck Pool meadow
Dragon of Brinsop.pullquote: Herefordshire's own St George legend places the dragon in the well of Duck Pool meadow at Brinsop.

Dragon of Deerhurst.alt: John Smith driving an axe between the scales of the Dragon of Deerhurst in a Gloucestershire pasture
Dragon of Deerhurst.caption: A visual interpretation of the Dragon of Deerhurst and John Smith
Dragon of Deerhurst.pullquote: John Smith drove an axe between its scales

Dragon of Mordiford.alt: Maud standing unharmed beside the grown Dragon of Mordiford on the hills above Herefordshire
Dragon of Mordiford.caption: A visual interpretation of Maud and the Dragon of Mordiford
Dragon of Mordiford.pullquote: she found a tiny serpent and raised it in secret until it grew into a dragon.

Dragon of Radnor Forest.alt: The last dragon of Wales sleeping beneath the dark trees of Radnor Forest
Dragon of Radnor Forest.caption: A visual interpretation of the sleeping Dragon of Radnor Forest
Dragon of Radnor Forest.pullquote: Beneath Radnor Forest, the last dragon of Wales sleeps

Dragon of St Leonard's Forest.alt: A low serpent with two great lumps leaving a slime trail through St Leonard's Forest
Dragon of St Leonard's Forest.caption: A visual interpretation of the serpent reported in St Leonard's Forest
Dragon of St Leonard's Forest.pullquote: leaving a trail of slime, and killing dogs and a man with its venomous breath.

Dragon of Strathmartine.alt: Martin luring the Dragon of Strathmartine toward a spiked ball of dough on Angus moorland
Dragon of Strathmartine.caption: A visual interpretation of Martin outwitting the Dragon of Strathmartine
Dragon of Strathmartine.pullquote: Martin lured the beast to its death with cunning and a spiked ball of dough.

Dragon of Wantley.alt: More of More Hall charging the Dragon of Wantley across a muddy South Yorkshire hillside
Dragon of Wantley.caption: A visual interpretation of the comic Dragon of Wantley ballad
Dragon of Wantley.pullquote: It is dragon-slaying with muddy boots and tavern laughter.

Filey Dragon.alt: The Filey Dragon among the tidal rocks of Filey Brigg with sticky parkin cake in its jaws
Filey Dragon.caption: A visual interpretation of the Filey Dragon on the Brigg
Filey Dragon.pullquote: its jaws seized shut and it plunged into the sea to drown.

Laidly Worm of Spindleston Heugh.alt: Childe Wynd approaching the sorrowful Laidly Worm on the Northumberland coast below Bamburgh
Laidly Worm of Spindleston Heugh.caption: A visual interpretation of the Laidly Worm enchantment
Laidly Worm of Spindleston Heugh.pullquote: A princess transformed by her jealous stepmother into a loathsome worm around Bamburgh.

Lig-na-Paiste.alt: The last serpent of Ireland churning beneath Lough Foyle behind an ancient iron cage
Lig-na-Paiste.caption: A visual interpretation of Lig-na-Paiste beneath Lough Foyle
